reference.note: React sources ported by spike S1 and lot P1 and measured in docs/preact-s1-spike.md. Same commit as scripts/port-metrics.mjs BASE_REF; verified no P1 source drift to origin/main.

ownershipNote: Lot P2 ports the 27 form modules (25 new here; Input and SelectableRow came from the spike and are raised to the P1 signal/style conventions) plus 3 P3 dependencies of TimeRangePicker (Menu, MenuPopover, ContentSwitcher) with their helpers (menu-cascade.ts, timeRange.ts). P1 (layout, action, feedback), Modal/Tabs (P3) and the P4c shells came before. Rows flagged hardSet belong to the P5 hard set as well and are removed from their category batch by the L1.5 overlap rule (PLAN section 2.9); forwardRef modules stay hardSet false because runtime.ts provides forwardRef on Preact core, retiring forwardRef from the P5 overlap set, so L1.5 must not strip them. menu-cascade.ts and timeRange.ts are runtime-neutral helpers like classNames.ts and internal.ts: emitted unchanged, owned by no manifest row. Lot P3 group 1 ports the 5 menu-cascade modules (MenuTriggerButton, OverflowMenu, Popover, Toggletip, Tooltip) with the MenuPopover consumer-style merge. Lot P3 group 2 ports the 12 navigation modules (BackToTop, Breadcrumb, Footer, Header, LanguageToggle, NavActionStack, NavItem, Pagination, PaginationNav, SideNav, Stepper, TableOfContents) plus 2 data dependencies of NavItem (Badge, ColorSwatch); the data lot is jointly P4a+P4b in the programme (spike section 8.3) while the manifest enum carries P4a and P4b separately, so the two dependency rows are labeled P4a. Lot P3 group 3 ports the 5 remaining P3 modules (Drawer, LanguageSelector, SkipLink, SlideIndicator, TreeView): Drawer is overlay, the other four are navigation. Lot P4a group 1 ports the first 16 data modules in manifest order (AnomalySwimLaneChart to ColorScaleBar; Badge was already ported as a P3 dependency) plus ForceGraph as a P4a dependency of ArcDiagramChart (its GraphLegend): 17 manifest rows, 16 new files and ForceGraph, whose interactive component lands in this group instead of group 3. Lot P4a group 2 ports the next 16 data modules in manifest order (ColumnPyramidChart to EventFeedPanel) with the cellDecoration helper for DataTable: 16 new files plus cellDecoration. Lot P4a group 3 ports the last 13 data modules in manifest order (FilterBar to ItemChart): 13 new files, closing P4a data batch 1 (groups 1-3). Lot P4b group 1 ports the first 16 data modules of batch 2 in manifest order (KpiCard to RibbonChart; OrderedList lives in catalog.tsx on the React side like CodeSnippet) plus Sparkline as a P4b dependency of KpiCard (its trend sparkline) with the priorityLabels helper for PriorityMatrix: 17 manifest rows, 17 new files. priorityLabels.ts is a runtime-neutral helper like cellDecoration.tsx and chartScale.tsx: emitted unchanged, owned by no manifest row.
adaptersNote: The three adapters are owned by lot P5 (hard set) and reused by every conversion lot. Their file set must stay identical to the ADAPTERS map of scripts/emit-react.mjs: the emission is the lint of the single-source rule.

adapters.note: K3: the only module importing preact/compat (createPortal only)
Core-only adapter: forwardRef, SVG presentation-attribute normalisation (options.vnode), insertion and external-store effects, textInput, textChange, focusWithin, dblClick, type aliases
K4: the only module importing @preact/signals (MaybeSignal, useValue, unwrap)

semanticMappingNote: Framework-specific props, events and slots of the port (PLAN section 2.9). Every row is a recorded difference with a test on both legs, not a divergence to fix here. The Vue side of the spike divergences (docs/preact-s1-spike.md section 4) is not covered: it belongs to the L1.5 manifest rows.

semanticMapping.preact: Props typed MaybeSignal<T> accept a value or a signal, read once with useValue (tracked) or unwrap (untracked)
semanticMapping.react: MaybeSignal<T> is T: the emitted props are the ones @sentropic/design-system-react publishes

semanticMapping.preact: Attributes spread onto an intrinsic element accept a signal natively, bound to the DOM without a re-render

semanticMapping.react: textInput(handler) spreads onChange (per-keystroke, required on a controlled field)

semanticMapping.preact: focusWithin(handler) spreads onFocusIn (native focusin bubbles; onFocus does not)
Events inside a portal follow the DOM tree and never reach a handler of the component-tree parent
semanticMapping.react: Clicks inside a portal bubble to the component-tree parent

semanticMapping.preact: useInsertionEffect runs in the layout phase (as preact/compat aliases it): a child layout effect runs before the provider effect
semanticMapping.react: Dedicated insertion phase: child layout effects see the injected stylesheet on first mount

semanticMapping.preact: forwardRef restored through the options.__b hook on Preact core (no preact/compat)

Intrinsic SVG presentation attributes are normalised to kebab-case by the options.vnode hook in runtime.ts (strokeWidth to stroke-width; viewBox, clipPathUnits and textLength preserved); tabIndex is normalised to tabindex on every intrinsic element so SVG nodes stay focusable

mergeStyle(base, style) in internal.ts merges computed declarations with a consumer string, object or signal style (signal detected via peek and read via .value, string concatenated, object spread with consumer winning; ButtonGroup gap wins)
React spelling className kept; a consumer class travels in the rest props and is replaced by the computed className

textChange(handler, onInput?) spreads onInput (native input event, per keystroke) for a consumer onChange destructured out of the rest props (Input, Textarea, Search, Slider, NumberInput, PasswordInput, TimeRangePicker custom fields); a consumer onInput runs first on the same event, so both handlers fire once per keystroke
semanticMapping.react: textChange(handler, onInput?) spreads onChange (per-keystroke, required on a controlled field) plus the consumer onInput untouched; the emitted module keeps both consumer handler references

semanticMapping.preact: Preact core (no preact/compat) does not re-impose a controlled checked/value after a rejected change: when the consumer onChange keeps value unchanged, the native control keeps its user-edited state (CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, TileGroup, Slider, NumberInput)
semanticMapping.react: React restores the controlled DOM state on re-render

semanticMapping.preact: Popover composes the consumer onClick after opening, Drawer composes the consumer onKeyDown behind the focus trap, Tooltip composes the consumer onFocus/onFocusIn/onBlur/onFocusOut/onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave around visibility, and BackToTop composes the consumer onClick before scrolling (order intentional in each case): the internal behavior runs and the consumer handler still fires once per event
semanticMapping.react: The emitted handlers are the same compositions; the hand-written twins drop the consumer onClick (Popover, BackToTop), onKeyDown (Drawer) and onFocus (Tooltip) behind the internal prop placed after the rest spread

semanticMapping.preact: focusOut(handler) spreads onFocusOut (native focusout bubbles; onBlur does not), so Tooltip closes wherever focus goes, including body, with no document listener; the composed consumer onFocus/onBlur now fire on bubbling focusin/focusout from any descendant like React, not on the host's own non-bubbling focus/blur
